newsitem.title: UK: EMI to return 499 mln pounds to shareholders.
newsitem.headline: EMI to return 499 mln pounds to shareholders.

text.p: British music company EMI Group Plc said on Tuesday it planned to return up to 499.1 million pounds ($816.7 million) of capital to shareholders under a previously-announced plan.
EMI, which said last month it would return about 10 percent of its market capitalisation, said the plan equalled 114.5 pence per share compared to its stock's closing price of 11.67 pence on Monday.
EMI's shares firmed 18 pence to 1,185 pence by 0925 GMT after rising as high as 1,220 earlier.
Under the plan, shareholders would receive nine new ordinary shares and five B shares for every five existing shares held.
EMI said in the process of reorganising its share capital, the ordinary shares would be split into two to improve their marketability.
The company said its final dividend of 22 pence per share would not be affected by the proposals.
"The directors believe that, in the medium term, the potential to grow dividends per share will be enhanced as a result of these proposals," EMI said in a statement.
EMI said it would buy back 120,000 ordinary shares on the market before the proposals were implemented.
EMI, one of the six companies that dominate the global music industry, has artists ranging from The Beatles to current hitmakers the Spice Girls.
